subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should SKILL.md metadata be allowed to declare scheduled or event-triggered autonomous runs, and if so what approval, provenance, revocation, and cron-registration boundary should own that behavior?
rationale: The implementation would turn skill metadata into an autonomous execution source, which affects public skill contracts, ClawHub trust semantics, scheduler state, and operator security choices that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Define Permissioned Core Contract
options.body: Approve a narrow schema and permission model, likely under metadata.openclaw, then wire parsing, cron registration, event hooks, audit output, docs, and tests together.

options.title: Keep Core Unchanged And Route To Plugin
options.body: Require a ClawHub/plugin implementation to own scheduling through existing Gateway lifecycle and cron APIs, accepting that SKILL.md frontmatter itself remains non-authoritative.

options.title: Start With Documentation-Only Metadata
options.body: Allow a non-executable trigger_description or audit hint first, while deferring automatic cron/event registration until the security boundary is settled.

recommendation.title: Define Permissioned Core Contract
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow schema and permission model, likely under metadata.openclaw, then wire parsing, cron registration, event hooks, audit output, docs, and tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans skill metadata, cron state, ClawHub trust, and repository product/security boundaries, and steipete is the strongest current-history routing signal across those surfaces.
